layers.name: OSNI Éire Thuaidh — Irish-Translated Map
layers.description: Bilingual map of Northern Ireland with place-names rendered in Irish (Gaeilge) alongside their English forms. Cropped raster cartography in Irish Grid TM65, served as XYZ tiles at zoom 6–12.
layers.notes: Georeferenced raster image overlay using metadata bounds and hosted image https://data.civgraph.net/data/maps/osni-raster/eire-thuaidh/{z}/{x}/{y}.png.

layers.name: OSNI Mid-Scale Raster — 1:10,000
layers.description: Topographic raster cartography at 1:10,000 scale across all of Northern Ireland — a 292-sheet mosaic of OSNI base-map tiles. Useful background context for site-level work; shows roads, settlements, contours and named features. Served as XYZ tiles at zoom 8–15.

references.label: OSNI Open Data — Mid Scale Raster

layers.notes: Georeferenced raster image overlay using metadata bounds and hosted image https://data.civgraph.net/data/maps/osni-raster/mid-scale-raster/{z}/{x}/{y}.png.

layers.name: OSNI StreetMaps — Town Sheets
layers.description: Detailed printed street-map sheets for 109 towns and villages across Northern Ireland — 0.85 m/pixel native resolution showing individual streets, building outlines, and town features. Coverage is sparse (only published towns are mapped); the rest of NI is blank in this layer. Served as XYZ tiles at zoom 8–16.
layers.notes: Georeferenced raster image overlay using metadata bounds and hosted image https://data.civgraph.net/data/maps/osni-raster/streetmaps/{z}/{x}/{y}.png.

layers.name: OSNI 1:1M Thematic — County Boundaries
layers.description: Small-scale (1:1,000,000) printed thematic map of Northern Ireland showing the historic six-county boundaries against a base outline. Designed as a wall-poster reference — re-tiled here as an interactive overlay at zoom 6–11.
layers.notes: Georeferenced raster image overlay using metadata bounds and hosted image https://data.civgraph.net/data/maps/osni-raster/1m-county-boundaries/{z}/{x}/{y}.png.

layers.name: OSNI 1:1M Thematic — Infrastructure
layers.description: Small-scale (1:1,000,000) thematic map showing major roads, railways, ports, airports, and other transport infrastructure across Northern Ireland. Re-tiled as an interactive overlay at zoom 6–11.
layers.notes: Georeferenced raster image overlay using metadata bounds and hosted image https://data.civgraph.net/data/maps/osni-raster/1m-infrastructure/{z}/{x}/{y}.png.

layers.name: OSNI 1:1M Thematic — Locations
layers.description: Small-scale (1:1,000,000) thematic map labelling major settlements and locations across Northern Ireland. Re-tiled as an interactive overlay at zoom 6–11.
layers.notes: Georeferenced raster image overlay using metadata bounds and hosted image https://data.civgraph.net/data/maps/osni-raster/1m-locations/{z}/{x}/{y}.png.

layers.name: Tellus Magnetic — Total Magnetic Intensity (residual)
layers.description: Residual total magnetic intensity (TMI) from the GSNI Tellus airborne survey — variations in the Earth's magnetic field caused by buried magnetic minerals (chiefly magnetite). High-magnetic anomalies trace mafic/ultramafic intrusions, basaltic flows, and iron-bearing sedimentary basins; magnetic lows mark sedimentary basins and demagnetised alteration zones. 35m grid spacing, ±3σ rainbow ramp.

references.label: OSNI Open Data — Tellus Magnetic Grids

layers.notes: Georeferenced raster image overlay using metadata bounds and hosted image https://data.civgraph.net/data/maps/geology/tellus-mag-tmi/{z}/{x}/{y}.png.

layers.name: Tellus Magnetic — Reduction-to-Pole (RTP)
layers.description: TMI corrected by reduction-to-pole, which compensates for the dipolar shape of magnetic anomalies caused by NI's inclined magnetic field. RTP places the peak directly above the source body, simplifying interpretation. ±3σ rainbow ramp.

references.label: OSNI Open Data — Tellus Magnetic Grids

layers.notes: Georeferenced raster image overlay using metadata bounds and hosted image https://data.civgraph.net/data/maps/geology/tellus-mag-rtp/{z}/{x}/{y}.png.

layers.name: Tellus Magnetic — RTP Tilt Derivative
layers.description: Tilt derivative of the RTP magnetic field — an edge-detection filter that highlights the boundaries of magnetic source bodies regardless of their amplitude. Excellent for tracing dykes, faults, and contacts. ±3σ rainbow ramp.

references.label: OSNI Open Data — Tellus Magnetic Grids

layers.name: Tellus Electromagnetic — 3 kHz Apparent Conductivity
layers.description: Apparent ground conductivity at 3 kHz from the Tellus airborne EM survey — penetrates ~50–150 m, mapping conductive saline groundwater, clay-rich soils, mineralised zones, and pollution plumes. Viridis colormap (low = purple, high = yellow), -2σ to +4σ stretch.

layers.name: Tellus Electromagnetic — 14 kHz Apparent Conductivity
layers.description: Apparent ground conductivity at 14 kHz — shallower depth (~10–30 m) than the 3 kHz channel, more sensitive to surface and near-surface conductors. Useful for soil moisture, near-surface alteration, and thin clay layers. Viridis colormap, -2σ to +4σ stretch.

layers.name: Tellus Radiometric — Potassium (K %)
layers.description: Surface potassium concentration from natural gamma-ray emissions. Highlights granites and other felsic intrusions (potassium-rich), alkaline volcanics, and certain sedimentary horizons. Inferno colormap (dark = low, bright = high), ±2-3σ stretch.

references.label: OSNI Open Data — Tellus Radiometric Grids

layers.name: Tellus Radiometric — Uranium-Equivalent (eU ppm)
layers.description: Uranium-equivalent concentration from the 1.76 MeV bismuth-214 daughter peak. Highlights uranium-bearing granites, organic-rich shales, phosphatic horizons, and mineralised zones. Viridis colormap, ±2-3σ stretch.

references.label: OSNI Open Data — Tellus Radiometric Grids

layers.name: Tellus Radiometric — Thorium-Equivalent (eTh ppm)
layers.description: Thorium-equivalent concentration from the 2.61 MeV thallium-208 daughter peak. Often correlates with heavy minerals (monazite, zircon) in placer deposits and resistate sediments. Rainbow colormap, ±2-3σ stretch.

references.label: OSNI Open Data — Tellus Radiometric Grids

layers.name: Tellus Radiometric — Total Counts (gamma)
layers.description: Total gamma-ray count rate — a summed proxy for combined K, U, Th, and other radionuclide activity. Useful for identifying overall radiometric "hot" zones before decomposing into individual channels. Inferno colormap, ±2-3σ stretch.

references.label: OSNI Open Data — Tellus Radiometric Grids

layers.notes: Georeferenced raster image overlay using metadata bounds and hosted image https://data.civgraph.net/data/maps/geology/tellus-rad-total/{z}/{x}/{y}.png.

layers.name: Tellus Radiometric — K/Th/U Ternary RGB
layers.description: The iconic radiometric ternary composite — K mapped to red, Th to green, U to blue. Reds = potassic (granite, certain volcanics); greens = thorium-rich (resistate sediments, heavy minerals); blues = uranium-rich (organic shales, mineralisation); whites/pale = high in all three; blacks = low overall. The most interpretively powerful single radiometric view. Each band stretched independently to mean ± 2σ.

references.label: OSNI Open Data — Tellus Radiometric Grids

layers.notes: Georeferenced raster image overlay using metadata bounds and hosted image https://data.civgraph.net/data/maps/geology/tellus-rad-ternary/{z}/{x}/{y}.png.

layers.name: OSNI Historical Six-Inch Maps — Edition 1 (1829–1835)
layers.description: The original Six-Inch-to-One-Mile County Series — the first complete topographic survey of Ireland, produced 1829–1835 by the Ordnance Survey. 308 historical map sheets covering all six Northern Ireland counties (Antrim, Armagh, Derry/Londonderry, Down, Fermanagh, Tyrone), engraved at a scale where every individual building, road, field boundary, and town feature is shown. Mosaicked and re-tiled here at 4 m/pixel for interactive viewing on the catalogue map. For pixel-level detail, download the original sheet TIFs from the per-county packages linked below.

layers.name: OSNI Historical Six-Inch Maps — Edition 2 (1838–1862)
layers.description: Second edition of the Six-Inch-to-One-Mile County Series, surveyed 1838–1862, providing the first comprehensive update to the original 1830s survey. 261 historical sheets covering all six Northern Ireland counties. layers.name: DAERA Network Contribution — SciMAP modelled pollution scores by river basin (26 catchments)
layers.description: Per-river-basin pollution-contribution scores from the SciMAP hydrological model (CEH Land Cover 2007 + Met Office rainfall + 5 m DTM), rasterised at 25 m and rendered as a Web Mercator tile pyramid coloured on inferno (low → high contribution). Raw GRIDCODE values of 58–100 stretch the inferno ramp from dark purple to pale yellow. Each parcel of land is scored for how much sediment / nutrient pollution its upstream catchment contributes to receiving waters. 26 catchment datasets were rasterised individually, mosaicked, and re-projected; per-catchment download links remain in sourceDownloads for the raw vector data.
